title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
authors: Tobias Schmidt; Rodrigo Gonzalez Laiz; Krisztián Szuppinger; Steffen Schneider
abstract: World models can achieve strong control performance without faithfully capturing the dynamics of their environment, limiting their potential for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery. Here, we introduce world2vec to learn mechanistic world models without reward information directly from observations and actions. World2vec learns latent dynamics that faithfully reproduce the true system over long prediction horizons, with at least one order of magnitude fewer parameters than DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and LeWM. title: WorldProbe: When Video World Models Fall Apart under Long-Horizon Spatial Exploration
authors: Minqi Wang; Jie Peng; Hejun Dong; Ruchang Yao; Puyi Wang; Siyuan Huang
abstract: Video world models generate future visual observations from camera or action inputs, with the goal of synthesizing persistent 3D worlds that can be explored across time and space. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate short interactions or rely on camera trajectories fixed before generation. The performance of video world models under long-horizon exploration with extensive camera motion remains under-explored. authors: Yuhao Lu; Jiongxu Chen; Hexiang Wei; Jiajin Wu; Juelin Li; Mingjian Liang
abstract: Predicting future physical states stands as a central challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations remain tied to specific robot configurations, and 3D motion prediction models use flow-only supervision, providing a limited learning signal for physical dynamics. To circumvent these limitations, we introduce \method{}, a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories. title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
authors: Liaoyuan Fan; Yuhao Zheng; Dongxing Mao; Hangyu Ran; Siyuan Hu; Weijia Mao
abstract: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. title: Tactus: Tactile & Pose Sensing Glove for Natural Dexterity Data Collection
authors: Li Guan; Rachael Granberry; Sahar Aseeri; Sahar Rostami; Taylor Niehues; Sai Dhanooshi Marri
abstract: Collecting naturalistic human manipulation demonstrations with accurate contact force and hand pose is essential for robot dexterous manipulation policy and foundational world model learning - yet no existing wearable platform provides both calibrated fingertip force sensing and occlusion-resilient hand tracking in a form factor that preserves natural manipulation behavior. title: Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception for Embodied World Modeling
authors: Haitang Feng; Zhuoman Liu; Zhennan Wang; Sheng Wang; Juelin Li; Chengzhi Zhao
abstract: Embodied world models should not only imagine plausible futures, but also perceive the geometric, semantic, and motion structure of the evolving world. We present GenSight, a unified embodied world model that brings future video generation and dense perception into a single pretrained video diffusion transformer. GenSight uses a unified spatiotemporal representation for video, depth, embodiment segmentation, and first-frame-relative 2D flow. authors: Huabin Peng; Fagang Jin; Yancong Wei; Tengfei Ma; Chuhang Liu; Chao Yu
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at instruction following, yet most remain feed-forward: they condition actions only on the current observation and discard both long-horizon temporal context and the hierarchical structure of VLM representations. title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
authors: Rongxing Ding; Hongyu Qu; Kehong Wu; Xudong Wang; Fan Zhang; Xinguang Xiang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. title: Generating Critic-Guided Synthetic Experience in Latent World Models
authors: Jorge de Freitas; Christos Ziakas; Alessandra Russo
abstract: Learning from offline datasets is limited in scalability, as collecting new experience is often costly or unsafe in the real world. World models offer an alternative way to generate new experience through a learned dynamics model, yet learning policies in latent space is limited due to compounding errors in imagined rollouts. To this end, we propose using the world model as a local transition generator, leveraging critic guidance to choose actions inside that model to generate synthetic experiences. authors: Fang Yu; Xiaoxue Wu; Haiyu Zhang; Yangfu Li; Botong Zhao; Yu Qiao
abstract: Long-horizon consistency is essential for video world models, yet it becomes difficult to maintain once observed content falls outside the context window. Existing memory mechanisms either retrieve history as implicit context, which remains constrained by context capacity and entangles static and dynamic information or consolidate history into explicit global representations, which struggle to model evolving dynamics and accumulate geometric errors. title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies
authors: Jiahua Li; Zixu John; Tom Zhong; Fuping Wu; Tianhao Xu; Ruicheng Zhang
abstract: A playable, programmable game world must maintain persistent state, enforce executable rules, and support extensible gameplay mechanics. Existing video world models can generate plausible combat, yet struggle to keep hit reactions and health updates consistent with game rules. title: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors
authors: Liangyu Li; Qingwen Liu
abstract: We introduce Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. At its core is a shared latent function space that captures the spatial and temporal structure of robot actions. We learn this space through two stages. title: Bayesian Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Latent World Models
authors: Xi Xiong; Lu Liu; Yiming Li; Jakob Foerster
abstract: Model-based offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) provides a promising approach to multi-agent decision-making under partial observability, where the global state is unavailable from offline data. However, limited dataset coverage can lead to substantial out-of-distribution (OOD) model errors, which may mislead policy optimization and degrade downstream performance. title: Assuring Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems with Foundation Models: A Neuro-Symbolic Agenda for Testing, Verification, and Runtime Assurance
authors: Xi Zheng; Ivan Ruchkin; Hong Jin Kang; Tevfik Bultan; Vijay Ganesh; Taylor T. Johnson
abstract: Learning-enabled cyber-physical systems (CPS), including autonomous vehicles and UAVs, increasingly incorporate foundation models, yet fragmented assurance practices provide insufficient support for system-level guarantees. We argue that restoring engineering control across stochastic neural, symbolic, and physical boundaries requires a shift from model-centric evaluation to system-level assurance. authors: Guancheng Pan; Qixin Tan; Yang Yuan; Andrew Chi-Chih Yao
abstract: AI has made remarkable progress in mathematics, solving challenging problems with machine-checkable proofs in Lean, yet typically relying on predefined mathematical definitions and formal specifications. This raises a natural question: can it reason rigorously about an unknown world? title: Agentic LinkDreamer: Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy World-Model Decision Making for Intermittent V2X Cooperative Perception
authors: Zhaoyu Liu; Dongmin Wang; Liu Cao; Jijing Cai; Kai Fang; Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed
abstract: Intermittent vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication can remove collaborator information needed for cooperative perception, degrading object detection during link outages. Existing recovery methods reconstruct missing features but rarely determine when to trust predictions, reuse historical observations, or request fresh information. title: Structural-Test Geometry as an Inductive Bias for Partially Observable World Models
authors: Todd Y. Zhou
abstract: Predictive world-model objectives need not organize latent histories according to distinctions required for later control. With privileged simulator access during training, should response-derived structural information be predicted, decoded, or imposed directly on latent geometry--and how do these choices compare with structured belief distillation? title: SaiVLA-JEPA: Evaluating Future Latent Prediction in JEPA-Conditioned VLA Control
authors: Rufeng Xiao; Ruihao Xiao; Wei Chen; Xinhai Sun
abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn to predict representations rather than pixels, offering a compact way to model how visual scenes evolve. We ask whether this predictive objective improves closed-loop control when a vision-language-action (VLA) policy already uses V-JEPA features. title: Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Evaluation
authors: Xiaofeng Han; Kaize Luo; Zenghuang Fu; Zichong Zhu; Zhe Feng; Changwei Wang
abstract: Embodied systems can update policies, world models, skills, and executable programs from deployment experience, allowing one interaction to benefit later tasks. When a system also revises and reuses its data-acquisition, feedback, or learning procedures, experience changes the process that produces capability, introducing recursive self-improvement. title: PulmoWorld: An Asynchronous Multimodal Medical World Model for Longitudinal Pneumonia Dynamics
authors: Cheng Tang; Xinyu Zhang; Jiawei Chen; Minghui Zhang; Shaocong Wei; Wei Li
abstract: Pneumonia changes across respiration, inflammation, and organ function, while the measurements that describe it arrive at different times and are often incomplete. We introduce PULMOWORLD, a world model for longitudinal pneumonia dynamics that connects asynchronous state estimation, recursive simulation, and evidence-constrained planning. title: Explore Where It Matters: Targeted Exploration for Efficient Rover Adaptation
authors: Jacob Levy; Arthur Bouton; Tristan D. Hassler; Hari Nayar; David Fridovich-Keil
abstract: Future planetary rovers will traverse steep, deformable terrain where slip, sinkage, and terrain deformation can threaten mobility. Although simulation can capture some wheel-soil effects, unmodeled deformable-terrain phenomena create sim-to-real gaps requiring deployment-time adaptation. Yet, rover operations leave little room for extensive trial-and-error. authors: Hayder Tirmazi
abstract: World models let observers explore and interact with generated worlds. Recent work shows that when observers revisit a region, current models often fail to regenerate it consistently. title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
authors: Rodrigo Gonzalez Laiz; Steffen Schneider
abstract: World models are widely proposed as core components for enabling agents to reason over long temporal and spatial horizons. Yet current evaluations often emphasize task performance while providing limited insight into whether learned world models acquire predictive latent dynamics that reflect the underlying structure of the environment. authors: Chia-Han Kuo; Chengshuai Zhao; Huan Liu; Lo Pang-Yun Ting
abstract: Time-series data play an important role in various tasks, such as weather forecasting, web traffic analysis, and speech recognition. Recently, pioneering studies have increasingly adopted Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) based encoders to learn time-series representations through latent-space prediction. authors: Jiaming Hu; Shi Bo; Yan Zheng; Tian Wang; Florian Dubost; Alejandro Mottini
abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) enable world models to plan from images by predicting future embeddings. However, their visual prediction objectives do not explicitly incorporate task-relevant state information, so the physical state that determines task progress may not be reliably captured in the latent space. authors: Haoyu Zhao; Yinzhou Tang; Zixuan Wang; Minghao Zhu; Dongchi Huang; Xingyue Zhao
abstract: Learning controllable world dynamics from heterogeneous interaction videos is challenging because robot embodiments use incompatible action spaces, while human videos lack native control labels. We present RynnWorld-Latent, a cross-embodiment video world model that uses the 3D-grounded latent actions introduced by RynnLAM as a shared conditioning interface. title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
authors: Hanqing Wang; Zhaotian Cai; Ruichuan An; Bohan Zeng; Tao Zhang; Yilin Chen
abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
authors: Brian Ko; Han Wang; Hejia Geng; Li Erran Li; Sherry Yang
abstract: AI research agents can propose, execute, and improve programs that solve machine learning tasks. However, executing each candidate program requires training and evaluating ML models, limiting how many candidates an agent can explore at each step. authors: Kang He; Wenshuo Peng; Chuanhao Li; Zihui Gao; Xiaojie Xu; Zhengyuan Lin
abstract: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. authors: Yang Liu; Xiaoli Liu; Liuzhao Li; Yuduo Song; Muyuan Liu; Xiang Gao
abstract: World-action models (WAMs) incorporate the prediction of future observations into robot policy learning. However, most WAMs build on billion-parameter vision-language or video-generation backbones, which incur high training cost and inference latency. title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
authors: Bingnan Liu; Ruini Xue
abstract: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. authors: Abdolrasoul Sakhaei Gharagezlou; Mehdi Monemi; Matti Latva-aho; Mehdi Rasti
abstract: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) have emerged as a promising technology for realizing large-scale antenna arrays in next-generation wireless networks owing to their ability to enable dense and energy-efficient antenna architectures. However, jointly optimizing digital beamforming and DMA element weights under time-varying channel conditions remains challenging due to their coupled effects on the received signal and interference powers. authors: Mattia Scardecchia; Sherry Yang
abstract: Video world models trained on large-scale robot data promise a safe and scalable approach for learning and evaluating policies that act in the physical world. However, they still struggle with long-horizon rollouts and out-of-distribution generalization, and they remain computationally demanding at inference time. title: TimeWorld: Towards Action-Conditioned Multimodal World Models for Time Series Forecasting
authors: Hang Ni; Weijia Zhang; Hao Liu
abstract: Time series forecasting supports decision-making in web applications such as online retail and network management, where planned actions can reshape future dynamics. World models provide a natural paradigm for predicting such action-dependent changes beyond extrapolating historical patterns. However, existing time series world models (TSWMs) typically rely on fixed, domain-specific covariate schemas that limit flexible intervention specification, while multimodal forecasters treat text primarily as passive predictive context. authors: Jiayi Luo; Yang Zhang; Liliang Chen; Nan Wang; Chen Gao; Boxiang Qiu
abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. authors: X-Era AI Lab Team;  :; Jianhao Lai; Zhihao Zhan; Zhiquan Liao; Qichang Li
abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. authors: Jingbo Xu; Hanchao Leng; JiaHui Huang; Hanbing Li; Jingwei Zhao; Kuiyuan Yang
abstract: World models are emerging as a fundamental component of policy learning for real-world agents, enabling agents to predict future world states and plan actions within a learned representation of the dynamic environment. title: Dream to Assist: Intent-Conditioned World Models for Shared Vehicle Control
authors: Jonathan DeCastro; Thomas Balch; Emily Sumner; Deepak Gopinath; Laporsha Dees; Patricio Reyes Gomez
abstract: Assistive agents in shared-control settings face a dual challenge: acting proactively to align with the human's intentions while remaining legible enough for the human to comprehend and fluently respond in real time. We present Dream2Assist, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for tightly-coupled shared decision making that addresses both sides of this challenge. authors: Akshay Mete; Dileep Kalathil; P. R. Kumar
abstract: Latent world models are typically pre-trained offline and kept frozen at test time, so planning with them can degrade under distribution shift. authors: Hanwen Cui; Yuanyuan Li; Qing Guo; Zhida Zhang; Chao Chen; Xi Chen
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) combine future-video prediction with robot action learning, yet improvements in task success alone do not reveal how predictive supervision manifests in execution behavior or whether its benefits persist under task and environmental shifts. title: Fovea-JEPA: Overcoming Geometric Blind Spots in V-JEPA for Camera Motion Recognition
authors: Xiangkun Shi; Hanhui Li; Shiyue Zhang; Chang Liu; Junwen Pan; Zhenbang Sun
abstract: Camera motion recognition requires separating viewpoint changes caused by camera translation, rotation, or zoom from object motion and scene dynamics. Video-language models often rely on semantic cues and struggle with the geometric evidence needed for this task. title: FlockWorld: Toward Population-Scale Multi-Agent Video World Models through Artificial Life Simulation
authors: Meryem Koksal; Yunzhe Wang; Volkan Ustun
abstract: Most action-conditioned video world models remain limited to a single player, while existing multiplayer models support only small, fixed groups of agents. We introduce FlockWorld, an artificial-life environment built on Reynolds's Boids algorithm for studying population-scale multi-agent video world models. Specifically, FlockWorld renders synchronized egocentric crops, assigns distinct colors to preserve camera-agent identity across views, exposes rule-derived accelerations as actions, and lets the number of camera agents be configured independently of the size of the surrounding population.

authors: Zheng Zhang; Xiaoyang Tang; Shuaiqi Cheng; Jiakai Huang; Zhongbo Wu; Ziyi Zhang
abstract: Robot policy evaluation informs deployment decisions and policy improvement, but physical testing and simulator preparation require substantial effort. authors: Lanxiang Hu; Yixin Huang; Abhilash Shankarampeta; Zilin Dai; Yuyuan Wu; Kun Qian
abstract: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. authors: Doanh Le Thien; Viet-Thanh Nguyen; Pham Tri Quang; Nhi Pham; Christopher Wewer; Minh-Loi Nguyen
abstract: Video world models (VWMs) are rapidly emerging as scalable neural simulators for robotic manipulation. authors: Zelin Gao; Hao Ouyang; Jiapeng Zhu; Qiuyu Wang; Jingye Chen; Zichen Liu
abstract: While interactive video world models require autoregressive generation, directly adapting pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into autoregressive ones with teacher forcing can disrupt their visual priors and degrade autoregressive generation quality. authors: Shuofeng Sun; Linqing Zhao; Haibin Yan
abstract: Video world models are expected to generate videos that accurately follow specified camera trajectories while maintaining consistent 3D structures. authors: Harold Haodong Chen; Rui Peng; Rongjin Guo; Lingteng Qiu; Kejie Qiu; Chao Xu
abstract: Interactive video world models require coordinated control over viewing perspectives, character actions, and camera motion. authors: Samuel M. Bateman; Tenny Yin; Chongyi Zheng; Lei Huang; Brian Wang; Benjamin Eysenbach
abstract: Action-conditioned video generative models trained on successful, goal-directed demonstrations tend to ignore the commanded action, rendering a plausible expert-like future regardless of what is asked of them. authors: Jie Wang; Guang Li; Zhijian Huang; Jinlong Li; Chenxu Dang; Hangjun Ye
abstract: Autonomous driving fundamentally demands dense understanding of visual, semantic, and geometric information, yet existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are typically trained with sparse supervision such as language instructions or trajectory signals. abstract: Existing world models can generate action-conditioned video from a single image. Many focus on camera movement, allowing users to explore the generated scene. authors: Adrian Remonda; Jiajun Xi; Nicklas Hansen; Marcus Greiff; Thomas Lew; John Talbot
abstract: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. abstract: Hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) relies on static spatial-spectral representations learned from labeled samples, limiting its ability to model structured dependencies in the latent representation space. authors: Youcheng Li; Fa Tian; Binbin Su
abstract: Simulating an individual's disease course requires connecting patient history to future events, clinical timing and disease morphology. abstract: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. authors: Weinan Zhang; Chunhua Shen; Tianfan Xue; Bin Zhao; Bingqi Jiang; Zihan Guo
abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. authors: Xiang Kaibo; Liu Qingfeng
abstract: Hierarchical world models plan over long horizons by passing predicted states from a coarse model to a lower-level controller. abstract: Latent world models let an agent plan in latent space. abstract: Streaming video world models generate the future chunk by chunk, conditioned on their own past and a stream of actions. authors: X. Feng; J. Tang; Z. Lin; L. Chen; S. Shao; Q. Lu
abstract: Building embodied agents that can perceive, reason, and act across diverse 3D worlds is a central research direction toward artificial general intelligence. Yet most existing work remains confined to specific tasks in a single scene and transfers poorly to new environments, leaving general embodied agents for open-world settings under-explored. abstract: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. authors: Zhaoyang Wang; Qianhui Wu; Haorui Wang; Simon Yu; Baolin Peng; Canwen Xu
abstract: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. authors: Zhiyang Deng; Yuzhe Wu; Zijun Lin; Yeying Jin
abstract: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. authors: Xinxing Zhou; Xiaojie Yuan; Yanlong Wen; Ming Jin
abstract: Time-series models increasingly condition on known future inputs. In controlled systems, some of these inputs are actions that can be changed, compared, and optimized before execution. authors: Karthik Iyer; Madan Dabbeeru
abstract: A retailer makes different decisions at different grains of the product, store and time hierarchy: store orders for an item in a store, supplier funding for an item across stores, category performance by store, and the financial plan for the chain. authors: Jize Wang; Yongcheng Jing; Xinyi Le; Cailian Chen; Xinping Guan; Dacheng Tao
abstract: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. abstract: Latent world models such as LeWM plan by searching for an action sequence whose predicted terminal latent is closest to the goal latent under an ambient norm, such as the Euclidean distance. authors: Lin Zhao; Bowen Chen; Qiaohui Gao; Shaowen Wan; Xiang Li; Wei Liu
abstract: Pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is a key prognostic indicator in aggressive breast cancer, yet existing prediction approaches either rely on pretreatment imaging alone, missing the patient's evolving response, or optimize multi-visit classifiers under direct outcome supervision, coupling representation learning with the clinical endpoint. authors: Kevin Chen; Yu-Wei Zhan; Haoran Liang; Sen Cui; Changshui Zhang
abstract: Reliable long-horizon prediction remains a central challenge for embodied world models. authors: Xike Xie; Yu Li; Weizhong Yang; Amalie Dyda; Shaohua Kevin Zhou

authors: Huanlong Gao; Xuelei He; Fengjun Zhao; Xiaowei He
abstract: Treatment planning is intrinsically counterfactual: clinicians must compare how a patient's tumor and survival would evolve under competing regimens, whereas a retrospective cohort records only the regimen received and one follow-up scan. abstract: GUI world models are increasingly used to improve action selection by predicting the consequences of candidate actions, but it is unclear how much of the resulting gain comes from prediction itself rather than from the evaluator that interprets those predictions. authors: Xiangteng Zhang; Haoyuan Liu; Yang Guan; Jingliang Duan; Yao Lyu; Tao Zhang
abstract: World models have shown considerable promise in sequential decision-making by anticipating the consequences of actions and providing predictive foresight for policy learning. authors: Yuze He; Bin Tan; Zelin Gao; Yujun Shen; Yong-Jin Liu; Nan Xue
abstract: Video world models that generate and explore environments at scale need a persistent 3D memory of what they have produced. abstract: World models provide robots with a predictive mechanism for reasoning about how actions change object states in manipulation tasks. authors: Botong Zhao; Fang Yu; Xinyuan Chen; Yue Lu
abstract: Lithography process drift can move a fabricated pattern outside its process window, producing unqualified scanning electron microscopy (SEM) morphology. abstract: Understanding and simulating how subjective cognition and mental states emerge, evolve, and shape behavior is essential for advancing artificial intelligence toward deeper social cognition and general intelligence. authors: Jiawei Geng; Zhenyang Liu; Yuzheng Wu; Yanwei Fu
abstract: Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects. authors: Yuxiang Ma; Weihan Xu; Pengfei Ye; Anna Mei; Yuxin Ray Song; Tingle Li

authors: Menghao Yin; Jiaju Yin; Xiyue Dong; Lixin Xu; Zhenhui Zhang; Ke Zhang

abstract: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? title: MAIA: Anticipating Interaction Anomalies in Contact-Rich Manipulation via Multimodal World Models
authors: Yi Qiao; Maolin Zheng; Haoran Sun; Lujia Dong; Wenzhao Lian
abstract: Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. Yet most monitoring methods are reactive, identifying anomalies only after they become observable. Anticipating such anomalies is challenging because visual observations only partially reveal physical interaction, while planned actions describe intended motion rather than their actual physical consequences. title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models
authors: Jiamin Shi; Yuanhong Zhang; Zhiyang Liu; Jiawei Sun; Jingwen Fu
abstract: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. We investigate the connection between action predictability, defined as the ability to reconstruct an action from consecutive latent states, and the preservation of intrinsic dynamics. title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
authors: Nicholas Saban; Charvi Bannur; Mariya Vasileva; Darshan Deshpande
abstract: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills. title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
authors: Hongchang Liu; Jian Liu; Yujuan Ding; Liang Peng; Xun Jiang; Fei Ma
abstract: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. title: From Optical Flow to Safety: Visual Safety Certification via Scale-Free Relative Motion
authors: Bazeela Banday; Jishnu Keshavan
abstract: Safe autonomous navigation using monocular vision remains challenging because explicit obstacle states are not directly observable. This letter introduces a visual safety-certification paradigm that uses scale-free, depth-normalized relative motion encoded by monocular optical flow as the representation for collision-risk certification, without reconstructing obstacle position, velocity, geometry, or a metric world model. title: DriveWorld3D Evidence Constrained 3D World Modeling and Generative Simulation for Real-World Autonomous Driving
authors: Wei Wang; Yiru Veronika Wang; Yihan Wang; Zihao Li; Xiaohui Liang
abstract: Three dimensional modeling for autonomous driving must continuously estimate road geometry, obstacle occupancy, traffic participant behavior, and observational uncertainty under limited computational resources. Existing reconstruction methods can synthesize realistic novel views, but visual fidelity does not sufficiently characterize the geometric reliability required for driving. title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
authors: Dongjie Cheng; Ruifeng Yuan; Ran Wei; Ning Song; Yongqi Li; Wenjie Li
abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) advance, they are increasingly expected to perform spatiotemporal reasoning over motion, actions, and view changes beyond what the input images show. Video World Models (VWMs) provide a natural unified engine for visual imagination by generating task-relevant visual content as additional evidence. title: When Reality Outpaces Cognition: A New Scaling Principle for Reliable Intelligence
authors: Ahsan Adeel; Talha Bin Riaz
abstract: This paper challenges the understanding capabilities of existing AI paradigms and emerging world models by asking a fundamental question: How quickly can reality change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act? We formulate this as a theory- and model-agnostic challenge in which systems must infer reliable actions for increasingly distant future states across a growing observation--reality gap. title: What Matters for World Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models?
authors: Qisen Ma; Yixiang Chen; Yuan Xu; Peiyan Li; Jiabing Yang; Kai Wang
abstract: Integrating world models into Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) has emerged as a promising direction, enabling policies to anticipate future dynamics beyond reactive observation-to-action mapping. However, existing approaches vary simultaneously in their world representations, integration paradigms, and policy backbones, making it difficult to determine what truly matters for effective world model integration. title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
authors: Chonghan Qin; Dongming Wu; Kaituo Feng; Jiaxu Wang; Xinlei Yu; Peiwen Sun
abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. title: Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series
authors: Shenyi Li; Ziyang Zhang; Wen Wu; Ming Liu; Chao Zhang
abstract: Video world models learn how visual environments evolve by predicting missing or future content. However, physical-state information can provide useful context for predicting how environments evolve. Prior work incorporates this information through different mechanisms: domain-specific physical laws can complicate multi-domain training, while supervision on individual frames or frame pairs gives limited attention to how physical state evolves over time. title: Tactile-Guided Robot Learning: From Representation Learning to Foundation Models
authors: Kiyanoush Nazari; Luchen Li; Haoshu Fang; Nima Fazeli; Zhibin Li; Fumiya Iida
abstract: Tactile sensing is becoming central to robust, adaptive, and dexterous robotic manipulation. Beyond its traditional role in contact detection and reactive control, touch is increasingly used to learn transferable representations, condition manipulation policies, and support embodied physical reasoning. Yet existing surveys largely emphasize tactile hardware and perception, leaving the rapid shift toward learning-based tactile manipulation insufficiently synthesized. title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
authors: Lorenzo Venturoli; Nedko Savov; Xi Wang; Marc Pollefeys; Luc Van Gool
abstract: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
authors: Zefan Yang; Zheyuan Zhang; Boris Maihe; Yikang Liu; Hang Yu; Ankush Mukherjee
abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
authors: Shaoyuan Xie; Zihan Zhang; Jingxuan Wang; Jiashu Qu; Xiaoqing Liang; Lingdong Kong
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. title: Pretrained Features as Teachers, Not States: Compact Latent World Models for Visual Planning
authors: Yanbo Wang; Nan Lin; Wendelin Böhmer; Javier Alonso-Mora
abstract: A key design choice in visual world models is what information the latent state is encouraged to preserve. Models that learn a latent space with only a latent-prediction objective adapt to environment dynamics, but the predictive objective alone admits collapsed solutions and provides no explicit constraint on the visual information retained by the latent. title: PAWA: Panoramic Action-conditioned World Modeling for Multiple Agents
authors: Siqi Yang; Yimu Wang; Ziqi Cai; Chengxuan Zhu; Shuchen Weng; Erwin Wu
abstract: A multiplayer world model must predict how the independent actions of several players change a shared environment, including changes outside a player's current field of view. A point-of-view (POV) video captures such changes only after they enter its field of view, whereas panoramic video records the surroundings in every viewing direction and has served as an intermediate representation of the world state in recent world models. title: One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models
authors: Joshua Cheung; Zhang He
abstract: Latent world models are routinely selected, checkpointed and ablated on one-step prediction loss, on the assumption that a model which predicts the next latent better is a better model. In model-based RL this assumption is known to be unreliable; we ask whether it also fails for latent world models, where the training target is the model's own embedding and the loss is not expressed in interpretable units. title: Neurosymbolic Learning of Interpretable World Models
authors: Riccardo Andreoni; Massimiliano Ronzani; Chiara Ghidini; Alessandro Daniele; Emile van Krieken
abstract: World models aim to learn compact representations of an environment from observations, enabling agents to predict future states and plan their behaviour. However, most existing approaches learn black-box representations, with limited ability to incorporate prior knowledge about the world. title: Model What Matters: Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling for Language Agents
authors: Maolin Ran; Minda Chen; Di Huang; Wei Xiong; Fei Huang; Weiwen Liu
abstract: Reinforcement learning provides a direct mechanism for optimizing task objectives in large language model-driven agents, but task rewards are typically sparse trajectory-level signals that only evaluate task success, without directly supervising action-conditioned environment transitions, leaving the model with limited explicit understanding of action consequences and environment dynamics. title: MemWM: Associative Memory-Enhanced Latent World Models for Long-Horizon Planning
authors: Yuwei Sun; Siyu Zhu
abstract: World models trained via latent dynamics offer a scalable path for embodied planning, yet existing methods suffer from representational collapse, computational overhead, and limited long-horizon capability. We introduce MemWM, a memory-enhanced latent world model that augments JEPA-style prediction with a content-addressable memory bank. title: EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos
authors: Meng Cao; Can Zhao; Jinjie Wei; Haonan Zhao; Yulong Zhang; Duo Han
abstract: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to costly robot demonstra- tions, yet transferring their manipulation priors to robot control remains chal- lenging. The commonly adopted retargeting-based approaches convert human wrist and finger poses into embodiment-specific action commands through hand- crafted geometric mappings. authors: Bo Li; Yue Yang; Yujin Huang; Siao Liu; David Lemphers; Sara E Rodriguez Gomez
abstract: Dynamic graph learning models how entities and their relations evolve from historical observations to predict future graph states. Existing methods do not fully address dynamic graph world modelling, which requires learning transitions from temporal context to future latent graph states. This is difficult for three reasons: nodes and relations rely on different historical evidence, structural evolution is path-dependent, and future snapshots provide sparse and realization-specific targets. title: Duration-Aware World Models for Sleep Staging with Dwell-Time Constraints
authors: Junhui Gao
abstract: Closed-loop neuromodulation requires sleep staging that respects stage-specific minimum dwells: stimulation policies switch by sleep stage, and a policy change is permitted only after the current stage has persisted for its minimum duration. Discriminative classifiers fragment stage trajectories---for example, a 30 s Wake segment inside a 10 min N2 run---and even hidden semi-Markov smoothing leaves 11.3% of segments below the minimum dwell threshold. title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning
authors: Colton Crosby; Hao Wang; Mac Schwager; Somil Bansal
abstract: State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own. Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. title: WorldOracle: Benchmarking Action-Conditioned World Models against Real-World Executions
authors: Haoyi Duan; Liliang Chen; Nan Wang; Yang Zhang; Yuhang Lu; Xiaotong Chen
abstract: We introduce WorldOracle, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) against paired real-world executions. Given the same initial observation and low-level action sequence, WorldOracle asks whether a predicted rollout reproduces what happens in the real world, including physical consequences and task-state transitions. title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models
authors: Nan Zhou; Jianxiong Gao; Qiuyu Wang; Wen Wang; Jiahao Wang; Yufeng Yuan
abstract: As video models enable longer and more realistic interactive experiences, maintaining a world consistent with its history becomes essential. This requires both preserving previously observed content and ensuring coherent world evolution over time. World memory is a critical capability to evaluate alongside visual fidelity and video duration. We introduce WorldMemBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating world memory in video world models. authors: Shangqing Zhou; Zhennan Jiang; Ning Ma; Xin Fu; Yupeng Zheng; Shuai Tian
abstract: Action-conditioned world models can reduce costly real-robot interaction in reinforcement learning for Vision-Language-Action models (VLA-RL), but hallucinations can mislead policy optimization. Extending them to richer VLA interfaces and long-horizon tasks raises challenges in spatiotemporal and cross-modal consistency, exploration-reliability balance in RL, and compounding rollout errors. authors: Haomin Wang; Anqiong Ji; Ke Wang; Zhongshan Liu; Ru Ying; Ran Zheng
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies excel at generalist robotic manipulation but generate actions without explicitly modeling their environmental consequences. World action models (WAMs) incorporate future prediction, yet most rely on costly video generation, while latent alternatives either use predicted futures only as auxiliary targets or infer latent actions from suboptimal visual transitions through costly large-scale video pretraining. authors: Jingbo Xu; Jianjie Fang; Zhuohang Li; Zihao Song; Zhaolu Wang; Xvyuan Liu
abstract: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. Although these models learn shared physical dynamics and interaction semantics from embodied trajectories, they are typically trained in isolation, which restricts knowledge reuse between prediction and control. authors: Thinker Team; Peng Gao; Jichao Jiao; Chen Liao; Daqin Luo; Yiming Ma
abstract: World models have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI, yet existing systems often remain fragmented in the modalities they model and the functions they support. In particular, visual dynamics, geometric structure, and executable action are commonly coupled through separate interfaces or downstream modules rather than being jointly represented and evolved within a shared dynamics model. authors: Yifei Yang; Zehua Fan; Zike Yan; Zhongyu Li; Yan Wang
abstract: World-model-based visual navigation enables action planning by predicting future states under candidate trajectories. However, long-horizon rollout remains challenging: models are often trained with ground-truth visual histories but deployed in closed-loop prediction, and evaluating many candidates with step-by-step rollout is computationally expensive. authors: Yunfu Deng; Sangwoo Shin; Brahma S. Pavse; Josiah P. Hanna
abstract: Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. These rollout-based approaches impose infrastructure requirements; simulator and world-model evaluators additionally face prediction errors that can compound over the evaluation horizon. authors: Xianglong Bao; Bosong Huang; Xiaoda Wang; Keqi Han; Carl Yang; Ming Jin
abstract: World models promise to learn how systems evolve and respond to actions, enabling simulation, planning and decision-making. Bringing this promise to biosignals requires more than accurate prediction of physiological recordings. We examine existing biosignal world models through two requirements for intervention use: a genuine action and evidence of its causal effect. authors: Binghan Wu; Kai Zeng; Kai Yang; Ya-Qin Zhang; Joseph Sifakis; Ye Ouyang
abstract: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. authors: Junlin Wu; Wen Fan; Dandan Zhang
abstract: Latent planners often rank candidate action sequences by terminal Euclidean distance to a goal latent. authors: Qihang Huang; Wenhui Huang; Collister Chua; Shiyu Fang; Zhan Chen; Songyan Zhang
abstract: Occupancy world models provide a structured, metric representation of future driving scenes, making them a promising basis for end-to-end autonomous driving. However, existing occupancy-aware planners typically couple occupancy prediction and action generation through either hierarchical coupling or parallel multi-task learning. authors: Jun Tian; Hao Wu; Ruo Chen; Yili Liao; Hongyi Lin; Jincheng Yu
abstract: Wheel-legged robots operating in outdoor spaces shared with humans require accurate perception, socially compliant navigation, future-scene reasoning, and scene reconstruction. However, existing datasets typically support these capabilities in isolation and rarely provide dense spatial and behavior-level supervision on real wheel-legged platforms. We introduce LynxScenes, a large-scale real-world dataset and benchmark collected with a LYNX M20 wheel-legged robot. authors: Wenxuan Guo; Yingping Liang; Zhaoguo Wang; Ziyuan Li; Angyuan Ma; Zhenyu Wu
abstract: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. authors: Henry Che; Xuanchi Ren; Sanja Fidler; Shenlong Wang; Laura Leal-Taixé; Shengyu Huang
abstract: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors. Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts. authors: Justin McMillen; Yasin Yilmaz
abstract: A robot's world model must remember objects that leave the camera's view. FloWM, a learned world model, keeps them in a spatial grid of features that it moves with five built-in velocities. title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
authors: Gennady Sidorov; Valerii Kornilov; Denis Grankin; Polina Fedotova; Aleksey Postnikov
abstract: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. title: From Pixels to Executable Physics: Behavior-Grounded World Models for Embodied Action Consequence Prediction
authors: Ruo Chen; Jiahua Pang; Yingjie Niu; Hongyi Lin; Jun Tian; Yang Zhu
abstract: In outdoor environments, varying terrain and contact conditions can cause identical action commands to produce different motion outcomes for quadruped robots. Predicting these outcomes is essential for reliable navigation and informed path selection. title: ForkCast: Predictive Recovery for Vision-Language-Action Policies via Counterfactual Futures
authors: Chenru Wen; Huajian Zeng; Haokai Ding; Jian Kang; Anqing Duan; Dawei Zhou
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies perform manipulation tasks using camera images and language instructions, but object slip or visual occlusion can disrupt execution. Recovery is typically learned during policy training or delegated to a monitor that triggers a scripted repair after detecting a failure. authors: Zijun Xu; Wendi Chen; Xinkai Wang; Jiachen Zou; Hongjin Chen; Hairuo Liu
abstract: Expert demonstrations show how to complete contact-rich tasks, but provide limited coverage of how interaction forces respond to different actions. Task-agnostic play provides broader experience of contact dynamics without specifying task goals. authors: Xiyang Wu; Zhichao Liu; Shengxin zhang; Zongxia Li; Ming Li; Tianyi Zhou
abstract: Long-horizon agents often struggle to recover from failures whose causes lie several steps earlier, beyond what local reflection or backtracking can resolve. authors: Shuzheng Wang; Haoxuan Li; Shengzhen Li; Chenxi Wu; Yajing Sun; Lu Hou
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and world models have demonstrated strong capabilities in semantic understanding and future scene evolution for autonomous driving. However, effectively integrating both capabilities for trajectory generation remains challenging. authors: Anton Arapin; Aditya Singh; Yixin Wang; Jun Gao; Bernadette Bucher
abstract: World models of visual information predict future image frames conditioned on given action sequences. authors: Jun Tian; Yingjie Niu; Ruo Chen; Hongyi Lin; Chao Li
abstract: Quadruped robots performing outdoor deliveries must interpret complex scenes, anticipate changes, and navigate in socially compliant ways. abstract: Humanoid policies trained in simulation can transfer qualitatively to hardware while failing to transfer the force interactions learned during training, compromising torque efficiency, load regulation, and robustness to impacts. authors: Junyi Wu; Zekun Li; Chenhongyi Yang; Chen Guo; Lingchen Yang; Yongan Zhang
abstract: Recent advances in video world models have enabled plausible interactive environments, yet long-horizon generation places a fundamental demand on visual memory: the previously observed world must remain consistent as the model continues to generate. authors: Shinseong Kim; Jaeseok Jeong; Jianlong Fu; Youngjung Uh
abstract: Video world models must generate physically plausible futures, not just realistic frames. authors: Chen Zhao; Zipeng Ye; Yihan Lin; Yuchen Xie; Jing Zhang

authors: Yaoyang Liu; Dongyu Yan; Yihua Du; Shengju Qian; Zeke Xie; Xin Wang

abstract: Clinical decisions depend on anticipating how a patient's condition will evolve as treatment is adjusted and new evidence becomes available. authors: Kaiyi Huang; Wangbo Yu; Yukun Huang; Jiwen Yu; Kunhao Liu; Donglin Yang
abstract: Multi-player interactive world models aim to simulate shared environments from multiple players' perspectives, but achieving robust generation while scaling to more players remains challenging. authors: Shatadal Mishra; Ahmadreza Moradipari; Nejib Ammar

abstract: Foundation models like V-JEPA are increasingly deployed across a heterogeneous edge-cloud continuum spanning smart glasses, phones, robots, and servers. Yet, they are typically trained as rigid, fixed-capacity networks bound to one device, supporting neither reconfigurable compute budgets nor collaborative execution. title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models
authors: Bahey Tharwat; Iman Nematollahi; Marvin Alles; Xingyuan Zhang; Akshay L Chandra; Abhinav Valada
abstract: Generalist robot policies are trained with imitation learning and are bounded by the quality and coverage of their demonstrations. Reinforcement learning can improve and extend them, either by fine-tuning the policy weights or by training a small module to steer the input noise of a frozen generative policy. title: Beyond Temporal Proximity: Explanatory World Models for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning
authors: Oriol Corcoll; Qiyao Wei; Ciarán Mark Gilligan-Lee
abstract: Generative Recommenders increasingly use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize outcomes that may appear hundreds or thousands of interactions after a decision. Standard RL propagates reward according to temporal proximity rather than explicit relevance, attenuating the signal assigned to distant but important actions and creating a source of sample inefficiency. title: Beyond Successful Robot Demonstrations: Learning from Human Interactions and Modeling Failure Dynamics
authors: Peiyan Tu; Cong Wang; Hanxin Zhu; Xin Jin; Zhibo Chen
abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a promising foundation for generalist robotic intelligence by predicting the consequences of actions. However, existing robotic datasets provide limited coverage of the diverse interaction dynamics required for generalizable world modeling. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer complementary interaction experience, yet the embodiment gap between human hands and robotic manipulators hinders effective cross-embodiment learning. title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution
authors: Ankan Deria; Komal Kumar; Hisham Cholakkal; Fahad Shahbaz Khan; Salman Khan
abstract: Video generators and video-based world models can synthesize plausible visual trajectories, but long-horizon procedural tasks require generation to adapt to what has actually been produced. A model must determine the next action from its generated state, execute that action, and recognize when the task is complete. title: WorldCast: Distributed Multiplayer World Models
authors: Ziyang Ye; Junchao Huang; Evelyn Zhang; Zhihao Xie; Ruicheng Zhang; Boyao Han
abstract: Multiplayer world models must generate independently controlled views with consistent representations of both players and their shared environment. Most existing approaches coordinate multiple players through joint multi-view generation, whose cost grows with each additional player. We present WorldCast, a distributed multiplayer world model in which each player runs a local client comprising a video generator and a state model. authors: Jiahua Dong; Anurag Bagchi; Yash Jangir; Muhammad Zubair Irshad; Sergey Zakharov; Martial Hebert
abstract: World models offer a promising alternative to physics-based simulators, yet remain far from practical deployment. We ask how far scaling ego-centric human video takes them, using a dataset of 30,000 hours spanning over 1,000 scene types and 14,000 contributors. Rather than relying on opaque downstream metrics, we directly evaluate agent and object-interaction fidelity on a challenging out-of-distribution benchmark. authors: Zheyu Fan; Yue Zhang; Mingkai Deng; Kangrui Wang; Qineng Wang; Canyu Chen
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning. We hypothesize that these failures reflect a shared deficit in visual transition reasoning, and test whether this capability can serve as a shared training primitive, one that different models can learn from different supervision sources and reuse across different tasks, with a systematic training recipe. title: VGGTWorld-VLA: Intent-Conditioned 3D World Evolution for Autonomous Driving
authors: Zhaoyang Liu; Kun Jiang; Ziying Song; Diange Yang
abstract: VGGT provides a strong foundation for geometry-centric world models by recovering unified 3D scene geometry from visual observations. Although recent extensions enable temporal 3D prediction, their future evolution remains weakly conditioned on driving intentions and actions, limiting their ability to model alternative action-dependent futures. title: UNITAS: A 3D-Native World Action Model for Embodied Manipulation
authors: Ruixiang Wang; Yongyi Su; Wenlve Zhou; Bo Yue; Hengyan Liu; Dekun Lu
abstract: World action models (WAMs) aim to answer a coupled physical question: given a task instruction, what motion should the robot execute, and how will that motion change the surrounding world? Most existing WAMs build on pretrained video generators and represent world evolution through images or visual latents. title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
authors: Denglin Jiang; Annie Wang
abstract: A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. We audit 113 works published from 1999 to 2026. 9 primary evaluations measure a real person's response to an action selected by the system or experimenter. title: Sign-Constrained Intervention Effects for Domain-Generalizable ICU World Models
authors: Zhen Xu; Nicholas Konz; Zhen Tan; Zachary Plotkin; Tianlong Chen
abstract: Predicting how a patient's vital signs respond to an intervention is a central question in intensive care. World models can do so by learning dynamics as a function of prior actions. However, such models tend to be brittle outside of training data. Clinicians choose drug dosages based on the patient's state, so the association a model learns between dose and outcome runs opposite to the drug's effect, generalizing poorly to out-of-distribution (OOD) dosing practices. authors: Jiaming Zhang; Xuan Wang; Fuyao Zhang; Yang Cao; Lingjuan Lyu; Wei Yang Bryan Lim
abstract: A login screen that appears after a tap on Sign in is expected; the same screen after a tap on View order is an attack. For GUI agents, safety is therefore a property of the transition rather than of the screen, and a monitor that inspects only screens can be defeated by reusing a legitimate one. authors: Shuang Luo; Yilun Kong; Yunpeng Qing; Yihang Jiao; Zhi Hou; Shunyu Liu
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a prominent framework for complex robotic manipulation, building on the strong semantic understanding of pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs). However, such VLM backbones offer insufficient physical dynamics priors, which limits the generalization capabilities of robot policies. title: RESETTLE: Robotic Recovery through Disagreement-Triggered Retrieval and Efficient Corrective Control
authors: Yuxin Chen; Senqiao Yang; Zixuan Wang; Jinhui Ye; Changsheng Lu; Pengguang Chen
abstract: Reliable robotic manipulation requires timely intervention to correct emerging deviations and restore progress after execution errors. However, recovery methods based on repeated vision-language reasoning or iterative online optimization can incur substantial latency, delaying intervention. To address these challenges, we introduce RESETTLE(Robotic rEcovery through diSagrEement-Triggered reTrievaL and Efficient Corrective Control), a model-agnostic framework that provides computationally efficient recovery at the action-execution interface of frozen robot policies. title: PlanWAM: Planning-Shaped Future Representations for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
authors: Jinchang Xu; Hongda Yu; Fengwei Dong; Wenhui Huang; Xi Wei; Yongzhi Liu
abstract: World models in end-to-end autonomous driving predict future scene evolution to provide foresight for trajectory planning. Existing methods mainly study how to predict the future and how to use it, but less often ask which future representation is actually most useful for planning. To this end, we propose PlanWAM, a Planning-Shaped World Action Model. authors: Yu Liu; Hetian Guo; Tianlv Huang; Ziyi Cai; Wudi Chen; Hantang Wang
abstract: Learning to predict how the world evolves can provide vision-language-action (VLA) policies with predictive context for long-horizon control, but its effectiveness depends on what future representation is modeled and how it conditions action generation. We introduce PLaW-VLA, which models task-relevant future states in a pretrained prediction-oriented representation space, reducing the need to predict control-irrelevant visual details. title: Multi-Agent Egocentric World Model with Fine-Grained Embodied Interaction
authors: Dahyun Chung; Siyoon Jin; Hyunwook Choi; Honggyu An; Junyoung Seo; Hyunsung Kim
abstract: Egocentric world models predict first-person observations conditioned on an agent's actions, but most focus on a single agent. Real embodied settings often involve multiple agents that act and interact within a shared environment. Existing multi-agent world models rely on coarse actions like locomotion, camera control, or discrete commands, leaving fine-grained embodied interactions underexplored. authors: Jie Chen; Ruofei Bai; Yuxin Cai; Yifeng Zhang; Chengyang He; Jun Li
abstract: World modeling has emerged as an effective co-training objective for robot policies, giving rise to World Action Models (WAMs) that jointly predict actions and future states. However, most WAMs predict future states in the native representation space of pretrained visual backbones, resulting in high-dimensional targets with substantial training cost. title: Mind the Temporal Gap: Evaluating Video Models for Temporal Understanding in Driving
authors: Shiva Sreeram; Erfan Aasi; Tsun-Hsuan Wang; Alaa Maalouf; Daniela Rus
abstract: Modern video-language models are increasingly treated as general-purpose video reasoners, yet it remains unclear whether they robustly capture temporal dynamics in safety-critical settings such as driving. We study this question through controlled ego-motion tasks that require identifying actions from driving videos. authors: Linkai Liu; Yuntian Zhang; Zhenshan Bing; Chen Chen; Lingjuan Lyu; Shangguang Wang
abstract: Direct visual navigation policies generate trajectories efficiently but do not explicitly evaluate their future consequences. Generative navigation world models provide this foresight through visual rollouts, which are costly when evaluating multiple candidates. We present LiteNWM, a latent navigation world model that shares visual encoding across candidates and jointly predicts their action-conditioned future representations at multiple horizons, while a learned scorer uses these predictions to select trajectories. title: Learning to Retrieve: Internalizing Memory Retrieval for Video World Models
authors: JiaKui Hu; Tailai Chen; Yuqi Pan; Xuerui Qiu; Jialun Liu; Xiao Cao
abstract: Video world models aim to generate explorable, 3D-consistent scene videos conditioned on camera trajectories. Existing approaches often rely on external memory systems that explicitly retrieve previously observed content to mitigate scene drift during long-horizon generation. title: LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs
authors: Minghao Fu; Tavis Siebert; Eryk Halicki; Randall Balestriero

authors: Shashank Hegde; Alexander Popov; Elie Aljalbout; Nikolai Smolyanskiy
abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict actions and future observations, typically from a reconstruction-based representation that carries noisy, redundant information which can complicate downstream predictions. authors: Zijun Wang; Zewen Liu; Minhua Lin; Zhaotian Weng; Zhan Shi; Bing He
abstract: AI research agents automate the cycle of proposing, implementing, and evaluating experiments, opening a path toward recursive self-improvement. Yet their ability to propose experiments outpaces their capacity to execute them in real environments, making outcome prediction a key capability for sustained self-improvement under limited experimental budgets. authors: Surya Shetty; Ulisses Braga-Neto
abstract: Large language model agents are being increasingly deployed as autonomous scientists, designing experiments and inferring mechanistic world models with minimal human oversight. Yet identifiability is often overlooked: when a plateau is reached, the agent needs to know whether it is not yet capable enough or the model simply is not identifiable from the data, in which case no amount of further experimentation of the same kind can help. authors: Boming Tan; Xiangdong Zhang; Yan Xia; Qi Zhu; Deyi Ji; Xue Yang
abstract: While recent video generation models synthesize highly realistic visuals, they lack a genuine understanding of intrinsic real-world logic. Existing methods attempt to understand the world by internalizing diverse world knowledge, yet constrained by computational overhead or dimensionality alignment, their learning processes inevitably compress features, causing a severe loss of structural information. authors: Janet Wang; Jiang Guo; Yi Xiang; Jiaqing Yuan; Mingwen Dong; Hideo Kobayashi
abstract: Self-evolving LLM agents typically improve how they act through accumulated experience, reflection, or skills. Yet even procedurally capable agents can fail when their beliefs about environment dynamics are incomplete, incorrect, or outdated. We study a complementary axis of self-evolution: evolving those beliefs during deployment. Such beliefs can support multiple tasks, but incorrect ones can also propagate across them. authors: Junyan Li; Ruizhi Li; Yu Liu; Xiangshuo Liu; Mingchao Sun; Hongyu Pan
abstract: We present DreamTrue, a multi-view, cross-embodiment robot world model for action-faithful and physically plausible video prediction. Training such a model on existing robot datasets faces two obstacles: imprecise calibration can impair action following, while limited coverage of unsuccessful interactions can bias predictions toward successful outcomes. authors: Prince Jha; Nils Lukas; Kun Zhang; Salem Lahlou
abstract: World models for control must capture which aspects of the environment respond to the agent's actions and which are relevant to reward. Generative world models such as Dreamer 4 consist of a video tokenizer, which encodes each frame into a latent, and a dynamics model, which is pretrained to predict future latents from past latents and actions. authors: Ziming Pan; Ruge Zhang; Haozhi Han; Junkai Zhou; Xingyuan Chen; Yifeng Chen
abstract: Atomistic simulation is a fundamental tool for studying long-term materials evolution, from diffusion and defect dynamics to interfacial reactions and fracture. authors: Tianhui Cai; Xinglong Sun; Chao Fang; Zhenxin Li; Rui Song; Jose M. Alvarez
abstract: World-action models have recently improved autonomous driving by jointly learning future scene prediction and trajectory generation. Most existing approaches model the future primarily through RGB appearance, and recent works have begun to incorporate geometric prediction to improve spatial understanding. authors: Feihong Yang; Xiang Long; Jincheng Yu; Jianfei Zhang; Guangjun Ge; Chao Wang
abstract: Robot navigation commonly uses wide-coverage, high-frequency sensing to reduce partial observability; this reliance becomes restrictive when another task temporarily redirects a shared sensor from navigation, interrupting navigation-relevant observations. authors: Ke Wu; Hanwen Huang; Bo Gu; Kaizhao Zhang; Xiangting Meng; Yupeng Zheng
abstract: World Action Models (WAM) improve robot policies by augmenting sparse action supervision with dense future prediction. However, much of the predictable future is dominated by appearance and scene persistence rather than action-dependent dynamics. We observe that several recent WAM designs, including optical flow, motion-centric representations, and latent actions, can be understood from a common perspective in which world supervision becomes more efficient as it contains a higher proportion of action-relevant variation. authors: Junwei Quan; Evgenii Opryshko; Nicholas Rhinehart; Igor Gilitschenski
abstract: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) has produced a diverse set of goal-reaching algorithms, yet no single algorithm performs best across environments, goals, and even different phases of the same task. Rather than deploying only the best-performing policy, we ask whether a set of frozen goal-conditioned policies can be used collectively as a portfolio, deciding at every state which policy should act. authors: Yanjiang Guo; Haodong Yan; Zhide Zhong; Zhongru Zhang; Qingyuan Yang; Qingzhou Lu
abstract: World action models (WAMs) have emerged as an important class of generalist robot policies, aiming to transfer video prediction priors to action learning. However, we find that existing WAMs frequently produce incorrect motion predictions in open-ended environment, leading to erroneous actions. authors: Keke Yang; Erqi Wang; Sainan Guan; Hongliang Ren
abstract: World models can enable autonomous ultrasound scanning by predicting the outcomes of probe motions from local observations. Learning this action--observation relationship typically relies on synchronized video--pose pairs, which are costly to collect at scale and largely unavailable in routine clinical recordings. authors: Yingchen Xu; Edward Grefenstette
abstract: Token-based world models enable fine-grained latent planning, but repeatedly processing large spatial token grids makes action search expensive. authors: Yatai Ji; Zhengqiu Zhu; Yong Zhao; Yue Hu; Fanglong Yao; Chen Gao
abstract: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object search involves a closed loop of perception, decision-making, and action under partial observability. Urban environments pose several challenges: large search areas and narrow egocentric views limit coverage, dense 3D geometry constrains safe motion, and open-world instructions require identifying a specific target among distractors. authors: Wenbin Teng; Tianshuo Xu; Depu Meng; Yuelei Li; Quentin Herau; Yihan Hu
abstract: Physical world modeling requires predicting how interactions change a scene, not merely generating coherent motion. authors: Artem Zholus; Nicolas Beltran-Velez; Jianhao Yuan; Sarath Chandar; Tushar Nagarajan; Daniel Severo
abstract: Latent world models have shown a remarkable ability to predict future states and to plan in the real world. abstract: Generative world models provide rich predictions of how manipulation scenes may evolve toward task objectives, yet those futures do not directly expose the compact task variables required by control. authors: Bingfan Zeng; Zhisheng Chen; Chenbo Sang; Zhengwei Xie; Jinpeng Wang; Xiangchen Guan
abstract: Long-term agents face growing storage demands as they accumulate experience. World models capture reusable regularities that can reduce the information stored for each experience. authors: Wei Huang; Bohan Zhang; Chenzhi Liu; Isabella Liu; Shuai Yang; Weian Mao
abstract: Real-time robot control demands enough visual history to infer motion and task progress, but processing that history can delay action. authors: Mayank Sengupta; Nirmit Desai; Eric Song; Kunal Sawarkar
abstract: Many applications of physical AI run within finite or closed physical worlds with a limited set of physical laws governing object behavior. authors: Yuchen Zhu; Chenyi Xu; Yulin Zhang; Gang Xu; Wentao Zhu
abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) predict masked or future observations in representation space, offering a natural source of predictive latents for vision-language-action (VLA) models. authors: Pranav Wagh; Yu Fang; Yue Yang; Mingyu Ding
abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is often built by chaining independently trained skills. abstract: Crowd simulation plays a central role in robot navigation, autonomous driving, and urban planning. authors: Leonardo F. Toso; Yann LeCun; James Anderson; Oumayma Bounou
abstract: Robotic systems often exhibit unstable modes, along which small perturbations and disturbances can cause unbounded growth unless corrected through feedback. authors: Zhihao Zheng; Mooi Choo Chuah
abstract: Safe social navigation requires a robot to anticipate not only the future consequences of its actions, but also whether a nominal action can actually be executed under surrounding physical and social constraints. We present Social-WM, an efficient latent world-model planning framework trained from egocentric RGB video sequences. authors: Jiajun Liu; Yifan Chen; Yichao Liu; Jiayi Zhang; Ruoqu Chen; Shaoxuan Xie
abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation reuses skills across many task compositions, but improving these compositions with additional end-to-end demonstrations is costly. authors: Benshan Ma; Pei Liu; Ruiguo Zhong; Lang Zhang; Mingyue Feng; Yaonong Wang
abstract: In interactive scenarios, an autonomous driving system is required to generate ego actions under the influence of other agents' behaviors. Existing World Action Models (WAMs) typically model other agents as components of the world model rather than as decision-makers that fundamentally shape the action of the ego agent, which impairs their performance in dense interaction scenarios. authors: Liming Lu; Xianzheng Ma; Wenkun He; Guanqi Zhan; Yilin Zhao; Junyu Chen
abstract: Video world models are expected to predict how the physical world evolves, yet they often produce visually plausible videos that violate basic physical principles. authors: Jingqiu Wang; Yan Wang
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently incorporated world models to provide richer dynamic supervision beyond sparse action labels. authors: Tingting Liao; Xuezhi Liang; Hao Li; Guangyi Liu
abstract: Streaming world models should render a place consistently across repeated visits. authors: Ali J Alrasheed; Aryan Yazdan Parast; Basim Azam; James Bailey; Naveed Akhtar
abstract: World Models are appearing as the next major frontier in computer vision. However, their robustness is currently largely unexplored. authors: Zijie Zhao; Shengqian Chen; Xiaoxu Wang; Han Jiang; Yuanheng Zhu; Dongbin Zhao
abstract: High-precision locomotion combines motion-command tracking with precise regulation of task-relevant physical states, enabling robots to interact reliably with their surroundings during motion. Joint end-to-end optimization can leave precision objectives insufficiently optimized, while reactive residual control adjusts actions only after deviations become observable. authors: F. Olivia Fan; Oliver Obst
abstract: Does memory-dependent control need nonlinear recurrent dynamics? We study simulated air-hockey defence under temporary loss of puck tracking. authors: Ji Xia; Tingting Liao; Xuezhi Liang; Hao Li; Guangyi Liu
abstract: When a camera revisits a previously observed region, a video world model should reproduce what was there before. authors: Wensen Wu
abstract: ARC-AGI-3 evaluates agents in interactive environments whose rules and objectives must be inferred from observation. title: JEPA-TTT: Persistent Test-Time Training of Latent World Models for Planning under Dynamics Shifts
authors: Zheyuan Zhang; Suyu Ye; Nakul Agarwal; Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub; Ehsan Moradi Pari; Daniel Khashabi
abstract: World models enable agents to plan by predicting future states of the environment, but their predictions can become unreliable when test-time dynamics differ from those seen during training. authors: Xiangyu Zhu; Jin Xu; Yue Guo; Xin Wu; Yifan Sun; Xiancong Ren
abstract: Video generation models (VGMs) offer strong spatiotemporal priors for embodied observation--action modeling. authors: Zijian Jin; Yunbei Zhang; Yuanzhe Liu; Ming Liu; Baian Chen; Weirui Ye
abstract: World-model planners typically scale outward by rolling farther, sampling more trajectories, or optimizing longer, while assigning the same computation to every imagined transition. authors: Florent Tariolle; Florian Yger
abstract: World-model agents are usually evaluated in simulators that can wait for the policy; live games impose the opposite constraint, requiring capture, prediction, and action before the next frame. authors: Morgan Byrd; Robert Wright; Sehoon Ha
abstract: Controlling an agent with vision requires being able to separate useful information from irrelevant background information. authors: Yongjiang Liu; Jie Zhang; Haoyue Zhang; Jingcai Guo; Deze Zeng; Song Guo
abstract: Equipping VLM agents with world modeling capabilities has shown strong potential for complex reasoning and long-horizon planning, while reducing the dependence of policy learning on costly real-world interactions. Existing methods mainly rely on prospective simulation to predict the consequences of candidate actions.
